文章介绍了一种名为Mirage Persistent Kernel (MPK)的编译器和运行时系统，它能够将大型语言模型（LLM）的推理过程自动编译成一个单一的megakernel，从而显著降低推理延迟。传统LLM系统依赖于一系列GPU内核启动和外部通信调用，导致硬件利用率不足。而MPK通过将多GPU上的计算和通信融合到一个megakernel中，消除了内核启动开销，实现了软件流水线，并重叠了计算和通信，从而减少了延迟。

MPK的关键优势在于其极低的延迟，尤其在多GPU配置下效果更显著。实验显示，在单个NVIDIA A100 GPU上，MPK将每token的解码延迟从14.5毫秒降至12.5毫秒，接近理论下限10毫秒。此外，MPK易于使用，开发者只需少量Python代码即可将LLM编译成高性能megakernel。

文章还详细介绍了MPK编译器如何将LLM的计算图转换为优化的任务图，以及MPK运行时如何在megakernel内执行任务图以实现高吞吐量和低延迟。

Star Quakes and Monster Shock Waves
June 03, 2025
Caltech researchers simulate a black hole consuming a neutron star
Across the cosmos, many stars can be found in pairs, gracefully circling one another. Yet one of the most dramatic pairings occurs between two orbiting black holes, formed after their massive progenitor stars exploded in supernova blasts. If these black holes lie close enough together, they will ultimately collide and form an even more massive black hole. Sometimes a black hole is orbited by a neutron star—the dense corpse of a star also formed from a supernova explosion but which contains less mass than a black hole. When these two bodies finally merge, the black hole will typically swallow the neutron star whole.
To better understand the extreme physics underlying such a grisly demise, researchers at Caltech are using supercomputers to simulate black hole–neutron star collisions. In one
study appearing in
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
, the team, led by
Elias Most
, a Caltech assistant professor of theoretical astrophysics, developed the most detailed simulation yet of the violent quakes that rupture a neutron star's surface roughly a second before the black hole consumes it.
"The neutron star's crust will crack open just like the ground in an earthquake," Most says. "The black hole's gravity first shears the surface, causing quakes in the star and the opening of rifts."
While cracks in the crust of a neutron star had been predicted before, the simulation is the first to demonstrate what kinds of light flares astronomers might see in the future when pointing telescopes in space and on the ground at such an event.
"This goes beyond educated models for the phenomenon—it is an actual simulation that includes all the relevant physics taking place when the neutron star breaks like an egg," says co-author
Katerina Chatziioannou
, assistant professor of physics at Caltech and a William H. Hurt Scholar.
Zoom In to Image
These three panels are taken from a supercomputer simulation of a merger between a black hole (large black circle) and a neutron star (colored blob). The images, which move forward in time from left to right, show how the intense gravity of the black hole stretches the neutron star, before the black hole ultimately consumes it.
Credit: Elias Most/Caltech
Image Lightbox
These three panels are taken from a supercomputer simulation of a merger between a black hole (large black circle) and a neutron star (colored blob). The images, which move forward in time from left to right, show how the intense gravity of the black hole stretches the neutron star, before the black hole ultimately consumes it.
Credit: Elias Most/Caltech
Download Full Image
In a second,
more recent paper in
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
, published March 31 of this year, the team used a supercomputer to simulate what happens after the neutron star fractures—a brief milliseconds-long window when monster shock waves, the most powerful predicted shock waves in the universe, shoot outward from the star. These monster shock waves had only recently been predicted by co-author Andrei Beloborodov of Columbia University. Now, the simulation, along with another from
a different study
published by the team last year, are the first to show how they form.
What is more, the most recent simulation does not stop when the monster shock waves form—it proceeds to show the neutron star being swallowed, which then triggers the creation of an exotic object called a "black hole pulsar."
A classic pulsar is a highly magnetized neutron star that emits beams of radiation, which sweep around like a lighthouse beacon as the star spins on its axis. A black hole pulsar is a hypothetical object in which a black hole launches magnetic winds that would also sweep around it as it spins, mimicking the appearance of a pulsar. While black hole pulsars had been previously conjectured, the simulation is the first to show how such a rare object could actually form in nature from the collision of a neutron star and black hole.
"When the neutron star plunges into the black hole, the monster shock waves are launched," says Yoonsoo Kim (MS '24), a Caltech graduate student working with Most, and lead author of the study on monster shock waves and black hole pulsars. "After the star is sucked in, whipping winds are formed, creating the black hole pulsar. But the black hole cannot sustain its winds and will become quiet again within seconds."

data.title: Estrogen: A Trip Report
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 本文作者Cube Flipper分享了自己在女性化激素疗法中的个人体验，并讨论了性别不安（gender dysphoria）的感受。作者强调，是否经历性别不安不应成为服用激素的前提，每个人有权选择在自己体内使用何种激素。作者通过自我探索，最终在COVID-19疫情期间通过自我管理的氯胺酮疗法面对自己的性别不安问题，并开始使用雌二醇贴片。文章详细描述了雌激素的生理作用及其对主观体验的影响，虽然其物理效果已有详细记录，但主观报告相对少见。作者还介绍了性激素的基本科学原理，包括不同类型的雌激素及其作用机制。最终，作者通过亲身尝试来验证这种疗法是否适合自己。

Estrogen: A trip report
Posted on 15 June 2025 by
Cube Flipper
Iâd like to say thanks to
Anna Magpie
â who offers
literature review as a service
â for her help reviewing the
section on neuroendocrinology
.
The following blog post discusses my personal experience of the phenomenology of feminising hormone therapy. It will also touch upon my own experience of gender dysphoria.
I wish to be clear that I do not believe that someone should have to demonstrate that they experience gender dysphoria â
however one might even define that
â as a prerequisite for taking hormones. At
smoothbrains.net
, we hold as self-evident the right to put whatever one likes inside oneâs body; and this of course includes hormones, be they androgens, estrogens, or exotic xenohormones as yet uninvented.
I have
gender dysphoria
. I find labels overly reifying; I feel reluctant to call myself
transgender
, per se: when prompted to state my gender identity or preferred pronouns, I fold my hands into the
dhyana mudra
and state that I
practice
emptiness
on the concept of gender
. Mostly people seem to vibe it, but sometimes it feels a little like weasel words. Other times, when Iâm in a sillier mood, Iâll tell people Iâm
genderfluid
â if only because it sounds like something Iâd put in my station wagon. Of course, my faithful Subaru Outback was made before 2008, which means it wants the
green, long-life genderfluid
â¦
I experience an ongoing
brain-body map
prediction error
â my brain seems to expect a differently shaped body to the one I wound up with. I have been acutely aware of this since before I hit puberty. Out of shame and embarassment, I suppressed this, but I also made a promise to myself that if I hadnât come out by the time I turned thirty then I was allowed to get as weird as I needed to.
During the COVID-19 pandemic I went through a phase of using self-administered ketamine therapy to refactor a long list of maladaptive behavioural patterns, and eventually this particular issue became impossible to ignore. I had avoided reifying it for long enough, and this wasnât working for me â I had to try something different. One evening in July 2021, I sat down with a close friend.
I am going to put a large amount of ketamine up my nose
, I said.
Your job is to start asking me questions about my sexuality.
Not long after, I had jumped through the relevant bureaucratic hoops,
and subsequently found myself cycling home from the pharmacy with a paper bag filled with repurposed menopause medication â a starter pack of
100 Âµg/24 hr
estradiol patches, to be applied twice a week.
While the
physical
effects of estrogen are
well-documented
, back when I came out I had difficulty finding detailed phenomenological reports of the
subjective
effects of estrogen. I did wind up reading a large number of anecdotal reports on
Reddit
, and found that in aggregate, people tend to report
positive subjective effects
. One could propose a number of non-exclusive hypotheses as to why â Iâll attempt to review these later in this post.

data.title: Extracting memorized pieces of books from open-weight language models
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）是否以及如何记忆受版权保护的书籍内容，并对其在版权案件中的影响进行了分析。作者使用了一种概率提取技术，从13个开放权重的LLM中提取了Books3数据集的部分内容。实验表明，部分LLM确实记忆了书籍的 substantial 部分，尤其是像Llama 3.1 70B几乎完整记忆了《哈利·波特》和《1984》等书籍。然而，最大型的LLM并没有显著记忆大多数书籍。文章指出，这一发现对版权案件具有重要意义，但并不单一地偏向任何一方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）中使用版权材料的法律责任和版权问题

不同观点：
• **[ai_legal_sus]** 认为LLM训练时使用了版权材料，并且模型的输出在许多情况下与版权作品有“实质相似性”（substantial similarity），因此应该对侵犯版权负责。该用户引用了论文和法律概念，如“提取即为记忆的证据”，认为如果模型输出与版权作品相似，就不应免于法律责任。

• **[Huxley1]** 认为LLM不仅仅是死记硬背，而是对内容进行压缩和重组。同时，该用户承认版权问题复杂，并表示法律需要适应这些新技术。

• **[Animats]** 关注LLM是否能够从训练权重中提取出特定书籍的文本，特别是像《哈利·波特》这样的流行书籍。该用户质疑是否因为这些书籍的大量粉丝材料在训练集中，导致模型对其“记忆”更为显著。

• **[andy99]** 提出LLM涉及版权侵犯的两个可能点：一是使用盗版材料进行训练，二是用户利用LLM生成侵犯版权的作品。然而，该用户认为训练过程本身不构成侵权，并指出LLM已经采取措施防止生成侵权内容。

• **[jrm4]** 强调如果LLM能够生成可识别的版权作品副本，那么这就构成了版权 infringement。该用户认为模型内部机制是否可见并不重要。

• **[landl0rd]** 指出，模型对《哈利·波特》和《1984》等流行书籍的“记忆”可能是因为这些书籍在训练集中被大量引用，属于合理使用（fair use）的范畴。

• **[w10-1]** 认为将版权法应用于AI是误导的，因为版权侵犯本质上是一种盗窃行为。该用户从原则上提出，购买书籍的权利不包括通过自动化手段进行复制或再现，并认为当前的法律和判例未能澄清这一问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于LLM是否以及如何对其生成内容的版权负责，特别是在模型输出与版权作品有“实质相似性”时。
- 讨论中还涉及训练过程中使用版权材料的合法性，以及如何在技术上防止LLM生成侵权内容。
- 一些用户质疑流行书籍在训练集中被过度代表是否导致模型对其内容“记忆”更深刻，从而引发版权问题。
- 总体上，用户对LLM的法律责任和现有版权法的适应性存在不同看法。

Title:
Extracting memorized pieces of (copyrighted) books from open-weight language models
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Extracting memorized pieces of (copyrighted) books from open-weight language models, by A. Feder Cooper and Aaron Gokaslan and Amy B. Cyphert and Christopher De Sa and Mark A. Lemley and Daniel E. Ho and Percy Liang
View PDF
Abstract:
Plaintiffs and defendants in copyright lawsuits over generative AI often make sweeping, opposing claims about the extent to which large language models (LLMs) have memorized plaintiffs' protected expression. Drawing on adversarial ML and copyright law, we show that these polarized positions dramatically oversimplify the relationship between memorization and copyright. To do so, we leverage a recent probabilistic extraction technique to extract pieces of the Books3 dataset from 13 open-weight LLMs. Through numerous experiments, we show that it's possible to extract substantial parts of at least some books from different LLMs. This is evidence that the LLMs have memorized the extracted text; this memorized content is copied inside the model parameters. But the results are complicated: the extent of memorization varies both by model and by book. With our specific experiments, we find that the largest LLMs don't memorize most books -- either in whole or in part. However, we also find that Llama 3.1 70B memorizes some books, like Harry Potter and 1984, almost entirely. We discuss why our results have significant implications for copyright cases, though not ones that unambiguously favor either side.

data.title: Testing a Robust Netcode with Godot
data.author: smig0
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在使用Godot引擎开发《Little Brats!》这款快节奏动作游戏时，处理在线多人游戏同步的挑战。作者介绍了如何通过延迟补偿、预测和 reconciliation 等技术解决网络延迟问题，确保玩家操作与服务器响应的一致性。由于网络代码不稳定，游戏发布曾被迫推迟两周。为了简化测试过程，作者建议在本地运行多个游戏实例，并使用Linux的`tc`命令人为增加延迟和丢包率，以模拟真实网络环境。Godot提供了高层次的网络API，支持选择可靠（TCP特性）或快速（UDP特性）的传输模式，帮助开发者实现稳定的网络功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Godot引擎在游戏开发中的网络功能、编程语言选择以及对开源工具的看法

不同观点：
• [fedorareis] 支持在多玩家游戏中使用可靠模式传输客户端输入到服务器，即使这会带来一定的延迟和服务器负载。他强调了游戏状态的稳定性和一致性，认为即便网络延迟严重，服务器也需要能够准确回溯游戏状态。然而，他也提到这种方法可能在极端延迟情况下导致不理想的游戏体验，比如玩家在明显移动后仍被击中。

• [ghushn3] 对Godot引擎的未来持积极态度，但认为GDScript是一个错误的选择，期待C#接口实现功能对等。他对Godot使用GDScript作为主要脚本语言持批评态度，但仍对Godot开发者社区的项目成果感到兴奋。

• [matthewkayin] 分享了他在RTS游戏项目中使用ENet和Steam网络功能的经历，指出Steam的网络功能提供了与ENet类似的特性，尤其是在可靠和按序传输数据包方面。他还提到通过抽象层可以在局域网和在线游戏中无缝切换网络库，而不影响游戏的其他代码。

• [sosodev] 认为Godot的核心网络代码过于简陋，仅提供了状态同步和RPC功能，并推荐使用netfox库来处理更高级的功能，如预测和回滚。他强调了在Godot中实现复杂网络功能的难度，并对netfox简化这些复杂性表示赞赏。

• [bee_rider] 关注文章中未提及的网络丢包率的乐观/悲观选择问题，表明他对网络传输中的丢包策略有疑问或兴趣。

• [righthand] 对游戏在Itch平台上以无DRM方式销售表示感谢，这与一些开发者选择在Steam等平台上使用DRM保护形成对比。

补充讨论：
• 网络传输中的可靠性和延迟处理是多玩家游戏开发中的一个关键问题，不同开发者对如何平衡这些因素有不同的看法。
• 对Godot引擎的编程语言选择存在争议，部分开发者对GDScript持批评态度，期待更多语言支持。
• netfox库被视为解决Godot网络功能不足的一个有用工具，显示了开源社区对引擎功能的扩展和改进。
• 游戏销售方式（DRM-free）也是一个值得注意的讨论点，反映了开发者和玩家对DRM的不同偏好。

2024-10-23
The biggest challenge I faced in developing
Little Brats!
was the
online multiplayer part: synchronizing computers with sometimes
consequent latency while maintaining the âfast-paced action gameâ
aspect was far from simple. I'll tell you all about it!
Lag compensation, prediction/reconciliation, etc.
I'm not going to do a detailed tutorial on these points, as there are
tons of them already, but to give you an idea of the principle: when a
client computer performs an action (in my case, for example, pressing
the button to slap another kid), the server will receive this action,
calculate what's going on, and send the result back to the client...
The problem is that even with a slight latency between the two
computers, say 10ms, you end up with 20ms between pressing a button
and receiving the result. It may not sound like much, but if you put a
20ms delay between each press of your keyboard keys and the execution
of the resulting action, you're going to lose your mind in no time.
In principle, this is compensated for by several techniques: in my
case, the client âvalidatesâ the action performed by default and
applies it in its local scene. This is a prediction. When the server
receives the action, it rewinds the game by the duration of the
latency (so, for example, 10ms backwards), applies the action, and
runs the game universe again for the equivalent of 10ms, all in the
background, without this being visible on the server's game. Then it
sends the final state to the client, which when it receives it will
either validate its own state if its prediction was correct, or
correct it if the server returned a different result (this is called
âreconciliationâ).
I'm not going to lie to you: it's very VERY complicated to implement
all this reliably and âinvisiblyâ. In other words, the people playing
the game have to be as unaware of it as possible, and there has to be
no camera âjumpsâ, inconsistencies, weird stuff... In practice, this
will always happen a little, of course: if your client had calculated
that you'd managed to hit a kid, but on the server that kid had
already moved out of the way, well, you'll see your action
âcancelledâ, and the kid will finally go as if nothing had
happened.
It was because of a delay on this network aspect that
I was forced to
postpone the release by 2 weeks
, because
my code was far too unstable, and in some cases the game was left
broken or in strange, buggy states. Anyway.
The thorny question of testing
Obviously, the best way to test a multiplayer game is with several
people. But in the meantime, when you're in the middle of development
and incrementing little by little, it's still necessary to test
âaloneâ behind your PC.
Of course, you can have several machines to test on, but it's still
relatively tedious, especially if you have to update the game on
all
machines every time you modify a line of script.
In short, the easiest thing to do is to run two or more instances on
your own PC and create a game on
localhost
. Godot makes it very easy
to launch several instances while keeping the debugger open on each of
them, which is extremely handy. All this already makes it possible to
test good communication between several instances, and that's no mean
feat. Except, of course, that latency between two instances on the
same machine is very, very low, and communication between the two
instances is 100% reliable (we'll never âloseâ a packet within the
same computer): we're not at all in real network conditions.
This is where a handy command (on GNU/Linux) comes in:
tc
, for
traffic control settings
. Let's take a look at this command:
# tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 50ms loss 1%
This command, run in
root
, âartificiallyâ adds 50ms of latency
locally, as well as artificially losing 1% of packets in transit
locally. In this way, we can simulate more or less degraded network
conditions while remaining on a single machine, and thus test the
robustness of our network code. Pretty handy, don't you think?
To remove this artificial degradation, simply do:
# tc qdisc del dev lo root
Godot, reliable/unreliable
Godot provides a high-level network API that abstracts from low-level
network protocols such as UDP or TCP. Here,
Little Brats!
uses the
ENetMultiplayerPeer
class, which uses the
ENet
library, itself based on UDP.
To explain the difference between UDP and TCP, take a look at one of
the many memes on the subject:
Basically, TCP transmits packets reliably but slowly, and UDP
unreliably (packets can be lost) but quickly. With its high-level API,
however, Godot lets you choose the reliability mode:
reliable
: guarantees the arrival of all packets in the order they
were sent. So we have an overlay to UDP where there's an internal
mechanism that checks the reception of packets and resends them if
reception fails. This can obviously be slower, especially on a
degraded netwo
44297656.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在使用Godot引擎开发《Little Brats!》这款快节奏动作游戏时，处理在线多人游戏同步的挑战。作者介绍了如何通过延迟补偿、预测和 reconciliation 等技术解决网络延迟问题，确保玩家操作与服务器响应的一致性。由于网络代码不稳定，游戏发布曾被迫推迟两周。为了简化测试过程，作者建议在本地运行多个游戏实例，并使用Linux的`tc`命令人为增加延迟和丢包率，以模拟真实网络环境。Godot提供了高层次的网络API，支持选择可靠（TCP特性）或快速（UDP特性）的传输模式，帮助开发者实现稳定的网络功能。
44297656.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Godot引擎在游戏开发中的网络功能、编程语言选择以及对开源工具的看法

不同观点：
• [fedorareis] 支持在多玩家游戏中使用可靠模式传输客户端输入到服务器，即使这会带来一定的延迟和服务器负载。他强调了游戏状态的稳定性和一致性，认为即便网络延迟严重，服务器也需要能够准确回溯游戏状态。然而，他也提到这种方法可能在极端延迟情况下导致不理想的游戏体验，比如玩家在明显移动后仍被击中。

• [ghushn3] 对Godot引擎的未来持积极态度，但认为GDScript是一个错误的选择，期待C#接口实现功能对等。他对Godot使用GDScript作为主要脚本语言持批评态度，但仍对Godot开发者社区的项目成果感到兴奋。

• [matthewkayin] 分享了他在RTS游戏项目中使用ENet和Steam网络功能的经历，指出Steam的网络功能提供了与ENet类似的特性，尤其是在可靠和按序传输数据包方面。他还提到通过抽象层可以在局域网和在线游戏中无缝切换网络库，而不影响游戏的其他代码。

• [sosodev] 认为Godot的核心网络代码过于简陋，仅提供了状态同步和RPC功能，并推荐使用netfox库来处理更高级的功能，如预测和回滚。他强调了在Godot中实现复杂网络功能的难度，并对netfox简化这些复杂性表示赞赏。

• [bee_rider] 关注文章中未提及的网络丢包率的乐观/悲观选择问题，表明他对网络传输中的丢包策略有疑问或兴趣。

• [righthand] 对游戏在Itch平台上以无DRM方式销售表示感谢，这与一些开发者选择在Steam等平台上使用DRM保护形成对比。

补充讨论：
• 网络传输中的可靠性和延迟处理是多玩家游戏开发中的一个关键问题，不同开发者对如何平衡这些因素有不同的看法。
• 对Godot引擎的编程语言选择存在争议，部分开发者对GDScript持批评态度，期待更多语言支持。
• netfox库被视为解决Godot网络功能不足的一个有用工具，显示了开源社区对引擎功能的扩展和改进。
• 游戏销售方式（DRM-free）也是一个值得注意的讨论点，反映了开发者和玩家对DRM的不同偏好。

data.author: RA2lover
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了cr.yp.to博客上的一系列技术主题文章，涵盖从算法分析到安全漏洞等多个方面。主要内容包括对Kyber-512算法"门"计数的分析，质疑NIST的计算结果；讨论Turbo Boost技术如何引发安全问题；分析McEliece标准化过程及性能和安全性；探讨量子计算机的能效及潜在问题；回顾NSA和NIST在后量子密码学中的角色；以及对双重加密、专利影响和向量化的讨论。文章还涉及了ROCA攻击案例、量子算法、随机数生成器、以及欧洲量子宣言中的安全欺诈问题。其他主题包括编译器优化、批量攻击的经济性及印刷系统的技术误导等。这些文章深入分析了各类技术挑战及风险管理策略。

Spectacle
Spectacle is an interactive, web-based tool for exploring, visualizing, and sharing formal specifications written in the
TLA
+
specification language
.  The motivation is to have a better way to quickly interact with a formal specification and easily share results. For example, it provides a way to share protocol behaviors and counterexample traces in a convenient, portable, and repeatable manner.
The tool implements a
full TLA+ interpreter in Javascript
, building on top of the
TLA+ tree-sitter grammar
for parsing specifications. This allows for interactive exploration of specs natively in the browser, without reliance on an external language server. A live version is hosted
here
, and below are some example specifications to try out:
Lock server
Cabbage Goat Wolf Puzzle
(animated)
Distributed termination detection (EWD998)
(animated)
Two phase commit
(animated)
Paxos
FlexiblePaxos
Raft
(animated)
Snapshot Isolation
You can also explore some interesting (and infamous) traces of different protocols:
Solution to the cabbage goat wolf puzzle
(Cabbage Goat Wolf Puzzle)
Raft log entry is written and later rolled back
(Raft)
Write skew anomaly under snapshot isolation
(Snapshot Isolation)
Read-only anomaly under snapshot isolation
(Snapshot Isolation)
Usage Notes
The current tool expects that a specification has defined its initial state predicate and next state relation as
Init
and
Next
definitions, respectively. If your specification has these defined under different names, they will not be recognized and no initial state or next state evaluation will occur. In this case, you can still use the tool in REPL mode, though.
Eventually this will be made configurable, but the current tool looks for these hard-coded definitions. Also, there is incomplete support for user module imports, so specs are largely expected to be written in a single module. The interpreter does, however, support most operators from the
TLA+ standard modules
by default.
You can also see a live demo of the tool and its features in
this presentation
, which also gives a very high level overview of the tool architecture and implementation details.
Running Locally
If you would like to run Spectacle locally and offline, you can do so by cloning the repo and running
make serve
from the root directory. This will start up a local Python server serving the app at
127.0.0.1:8000
.
Testing
Currently, nearly all testing of the tool is done via conformance testing against TLC. That is, for a given specification, we
generate its reachable state graph using TLC
and compare this for equivalence against the reachable state graph generated by the Javascript interpreter. You can see the result of all current tests that are run on
this page
, and the underlying test specs
here
.

data.title: Double-Entry Ledgers: The Missing Primitive in Modern Software
data.author: pgr0ss
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了双 entries 记账模型在软件开发中的未充分利用，并介绍了一个名为 "pgledger" 的纯 PostgreSQL 实现。双 entries 记账包含几个核心概念：当前余额、余额变化的历史记录以及资金来源。这种模型通过原子性的记录确保数据的一致性和错误检查，同时提供审计日志功能。

文章以在线业务为例，展示了如何使用双 entries 记账来记录订单、付款和退款。通过这种方法，可以明确记录每个资金转移，并方便地回答如“我们还在等多少钱？”或“为什么余额不对？”等问题。相比传统单表记录方式，双 entries 记账能更清晰地追踪资金流动，减少自定义错误检查逻辑的需要。

总的来说，文章提倡在更多系统中使用双 entries 记账，以提高数据一致性和可追溯性。

I think ledgers are underutilized in software development today. Specifically,
double-entry ledger
modeling would be a better fit in a lot of systems than the ad-hoc ledger-ish things they currently have.
This is why Iâve been working on
pgledger
, a pure PostgreSQL ledger implementation. If adding a ledger implementation is super simple, then Iâm hoping more folks will do it. And it can become another modeling primitive that we reach for to accomplish all sorts of things.
What is a Ledger?
A double-entry ledger at its core is a few simple concepts put together:
The current amount or balance of a thing
A historical record of how the amount got to that amount (immutable, append only, etc)
Where that amount came from at each step
Thatâs it. So if Alice sends $100 to Bob, the ledger records Aliceâs balance changing from $0 to $-100 (going to Bob) and Bobâs balance changing from $0 to $100 (coming from Alice). All of this is recorded at once, all amounts are accounted for, and all balances sum to $0.
Note:
Many ledgers model debits and credits rather than negative and positive numbers. In this case, Alice would have a debit of $100 and Bob would have a credit of $100. Personally, I find using negative and positive numbers simpler.
1
The fact that every transfer only moves amounts, never creates them from scratch, is a built-in error check.
2
And the historical record serves as an audit log.
How the ledger is implemented and what is actually stored on disk varies with each ledger implementation, but the important point is that all of this information is recorded atomically.
Once you start thinking about tracking amount changes over time, you start seeing ledgers in more places. Letâs walk through some examples Iâve seen in real software.
Recording Payments
Say we are building an online business. Starting simple, we need to know when someone places an order, so maybe we start with an
orders
table. But then we realize that payments have a more complicated lifecycle (we donât receive the payment right away when an order is created), so we want to know when we can actually start service or ship a product. We might add a
payments
table with a
status
column that represents values like
waiting_to_receive
or
complete
.
This is sort of like a single entry ledger. We have a table of âtransfersâ from customers to our business. But things soon get more complicated. How do we record a refund? Is that a new
refunds
table? Or do we record a row in
payments
with a negative amount? What happens when our account balance isnât what we expect? Are we missing payments? Or did we receive a different amount than we expected? How can we figure it out?
If we have a real double-entry ledger, we can record these interactions more explicitly:
When an order is created, we now have a
receivable
, where we are waiting on money. We can represent this as a transfer from the external user to a
receivables

We can also easily answer questions like âhow much money are we waiting for?â without any extra logic (the balance of the

文章主要讨论了双 entries 记账模型在软件开发中的未充分利用，并介绍了一个名为 "pgledger" 的纯 PostgreSQL 实现。双 entries 记账包含几个核心概念：当前余额、余额变化的历史记录以及资金来源。这种模型通过原子性的记录确保数据的一致性和错误检查，同时提供审计日志功能。

文章以在线业务为例，展示了如何使用双 entries 记账来记录订单、付款和退款。通过这种方法，可以明确记录每个资金转移，并方便地回答如“我们还在等多少钱？”或“为什么余额不对？”等问题。相比传统单表记录方式，双 entries 记账能更清晰地追踪资金流动，减少自定义错误检查逻辑的需要。

总的来说，文章提倡在更多系统中使用双 entries 记账，以提高数据一致性和可追溯性。

data.title: Show HN: Workout.cool – Open-source fitness coaching platform
data.author: surgomat
data.article_summary: **Workout.cool** 是一个开源的现代健身指导平台，提供创建训练计划、跟踪进度以及访问包含详细说明和视频演示的综合运动数据库的功能。该项目源于对之前平台 **workout.lol** 的复兴和改进。原项目由于与视频提供商的合作问题和高昂的授权成本而被出售并最终废弃。为了不让有价值的项目消失，主要贡献者决定重新创建 **workout.cool**，旨在为开源健身社区提供可靠、现代且易于维护的平台。项目提供了快速入门指南、综合运动数据库导入功能以及详细的架构说明，并欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源健身应用的功能、可用性、技术问题及改进建议

不同观点：
• **Vincenius**（原作者）：对应用被再次维护感到高兴，并肯定了UI的改进。提到曾尝试联系现拥有者但未果。
• **minimalist**：遇到错误信息（"error loading exercises"），并提到wger项目作为一个已有近十年历史的FLOSS自托管解决方案，具有多用户支持和跨平台特性，但其锻炼数据库不够全面，鼓励贡献。
• **toyetic**：认为应用对新手有帮助，但高级用户更关心持续的跟踪功能。建议增加移动应用和保存/跟踪长期锻炼计划的功能。
• **olliejennings**：提供了一个开放的锻炼数据库API和数据集，可能对解决数据问题有帮助。
• **Eric_WVGG**：认为缺少关于举重次数和重量的建议，并提出类似"100 Pushups"程序的算法建议，愿意贡献UI和功能。
• **nerevarthelame**：遇到多个技术问题，认为锻炼推荐算法缺乏对健身计划设计的理解，建议专注于记录现有锻炼和导入他人设计的计划。
• **adobrawy**：遇到具体的API请求错误，并提供了详细的错误信息和请求日志。
• **midenginedcoupe**：提到Stronger By Science的免费程序包，可能有助于解决应用中的锻炼选择和编程问题。
• **Sander_Marechal**：建议不要强制选择设备和肌肉群，而是提供初学者过滤选项。
• **pwillia7**：对workout.lol的视频恢复表示高兴。
• **lorepieri**：推荐了bodyweightfitness的wiki和会话跟踪表。
• **stephenhandley**：对选择肌肉群的功能感到困惑，但对开源健身项目本身表示支持。
• **zeta0134**：作为新手，对复杂的肌肉选择界面感到困惑，建议为初学者提供更友好的推荐。
• **FinnKuhn**：建议增加难度/力量设置，以适应不同用户的能力。
• **gregwebs**：提到Liftosaur项目，一个可编程和共享的举重跟踪应用，具有链接YouTube视频的锻炼数据库。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要在于锻炼推荐算法的实用性和准确性，特别是对不同用户群体（新手和高级用户）的需求差异。
• 技术问题集中在API错误和数据加载问题上，部分用户提供了具体的错误信息和可能的解决方案。
• 用户普遍希望增加移动应用支持、保存锻炼计划功能、以及更友好的用户界面和推荐系统。
• 开源贡献和社区支持被多次提到，作为解决数据库不足和锻炼推荐问题的潜在途径。

About
A comprehensive fitness coaching platform that allows create workout plans for you, track progress, and access a vast exercise database with
detailed instructions and video demonstrations.
🎯 Project Origin & Motivation
This project was born from a personal mission to revive and improve upon a previous fitness platform. As the
primary contributor
to the
original
workout.lol
project, I witnessed its journey and abandonment. 🥹
The Story Behind
workout.cool
🏗️
Original Contributor
: I was the main contributor to workout.lol
💼
Business Challenges
: The original project faced major hurdles with exercise video partnerships (no reliable video provider) could
be established
💰
Project Sale
: Due to these partnership issues, the project was sold to another party
📉
Abandonment
: The new owner quickly realized that
exercise video licensing costs were prohibitively expensive
, began to be sick
and abandoned the entire project
🔄
Revival Attempts
: For the past
9 months
, I've been trying to reconnect with the new stakeholder
📧
Radio Silence
: Despite multiple (15) attempts, there has been no response
🚀
New Beginning
: Rather than let this valuable work disappear, I decided to create a fresh, modern implementation
Why
workout.cool
Exists
Someone had to step up.
The opensource fitness community deserves better than broken promises and abandoned platforms.
I'm not building this for profit.
This isn't just a revival : it's an evolution.
workout.cool
represents everything the original project could have been, with the
reliability, modern approach, and
maintenance
that the fitness open source community deserves.
👥 From the Community, For the Community
I'm not just a developer : I'm a user who refused to let our community down.
I experienced firsthand the frustration of watching a beloved tool slowly disappear. Like many of you, I had workouts saved, progress
tracked, and a routine built around the platform.
My Mission: Rescue & Revive.
If you were part of the original workout.lol community, welcome back! If you're new here, welcome to the future of fitness platform
management.

make dev
This will start the database in Docker, run migrations, seed the DB, and start the Next.js dev server.
To stop services run
make down
Open your browser

data.title: Eliza: The doll that teaches girls to code
data.author: yz-exodao
data.article_summary: Eliza是一款专为女孩设计的智能娃娃，通过结合硬件和软件的技术项目帮助她们学习编程，同时保持趣味性。娃娃配备脉搏传感器、颜色传感器和土壤传感器等，可以检测心跳、变色以搭配孩子服饰，以及测试植物是否需要浇水。通过三个简单步骤，女孩们可以与Eliza互动、学习并享受编程乐趣。这款娃娃旨在缩小科技领域的性别差距，激励更多女孩进入STEM（科学、技术、工程、数学）领域。Eliza的创造者Eliza Kosoy是加州大学伯克利分校的博士生，她希望通过这款娃娃激发女孩对科技的兴趣，培养新一代女性科学家，改变科技行业格局。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程娃娃是否能帮助缩小科技行业的性别差距，以及其对儿童兴趣的影响

不同观点：
• [pathartl的观点] 认为编程娃娃并不是解决女性在科技行业中代表性不足问题的关键。他质疑这种做法是否能真正“解决性别差距”，并指出自己的朋友的女儿通过参加LEGO联盟同样获得了乐趣，表明女孩和男孩在科技活动中可以享有相同的乐趣。他还批评了将娃娃与女孩、汽车与男孩关联的刻板印象，主张不应预设性别偏好。

• [vunderba的观点] 更关注技术实现，将编程娃娃与嵌入Adafruit Playground Express的技术相比较，提到类似Iron Man的技术风格。他根据截图推测娃娃可能使用类似MakeCode的块编辑器，类似于Scratch，表明其技术背景和关注点在于玩具的技术细节和实现方式。

• [pathartl] 强调不应通过预设性别化的玩具来影响孩子的兴趣，而应提供更开放的选择，避免性别刻板印象。

Dolls that teach girls how to code, because girls just want to have fun, and learn to code.
SCROLL TO LEARN ABOUT THE DOLL OF THE FUTURE
↓
A DOLL THAT TEACHES GIRLS HOW TO CODE
Eliza teaches young girls how to code and build hardware through custom, tech-enabled projects based on things girls love.
ELIZA IS MADE WITH EASY-TO-LEARN TECHNOLOGY
STEP ONE
Plug in your hardware and attach it to Eliza.

Watch how Eliza responds to your code projects.
STEP THREE
Play, learn, and have fun with Eliza!
ELIZA MAKES LEARNING FUN
Eliza wants to travel to space when she grows up. She can show you her interplanetary tricks.
ELIZA CAN DETECT THE TRUTH

ELIZA ALWAYS MATCHES YOUR OUTFIT
Hold up your outfit to the color sensor and the Eliza’s dress and accessories will turn that color, so she matches you! E-liza uses this to camouflage on other planets in case of aliens.
ELIZA UNDERSTANDS PLANTS
Place the soil sensor into various plants around your house to see which need water. Eliza uses this to find water on other planets.
PLAY TODAY, CHANGE TOMORROW
Eliza will fix the gender diversity gap and create
a new generation of
women in STEM.
We want to expose young girls to technological concepts and encourage creative thinking through hardware and software, preventing girls from being influenced by generational stereotypes.
No product on the market targets the natural interest of girls, combined with technology. Parents have so few options, they feel they need to force their daughters to play with STEM products designed for boys, in order to get their daughters on a STEM path.
We believe little girls don’t have to sacrifice their interests in order to play with educational STEM toys.
Mark Zuckerberg, Bill Gates, Elon Musk, Sergei Brin (founder of Google), and many other technology leaders all started tinkering with computers at a young age. Now girls of today’s generation will too.
THE BIG IDEA BEHIND ELIZA
Meet Eliza. The human one.
Eliza Kosoy is a PhD student at UC Berkeley working in child development and Artificial Intelligence working with Prof. Alison Gopnik, previously she worked at MIT. She has worked as a data analyst, coached a LEGO robotics team and hosted a local TV show where sassy children debated the intellectual elite such as Nobel Prize winners.
During her time in various computational labs and start-ups she couldn’t help but notice how few women and POC surrounded her, she set out to change that with Eliza dolls! Our mission is to spark curiosity and wonder in the hearts of young girls and inspire their confidence in STEM engineering. Eliza will enable a new generation of women scientists that will fundamentally change the balance of power in technology and create better products for society.
ELIZA SIMPLY MAKES LEARNING FUN
In 2018, women made up only 28%
of the science and engineering workforce.
Let’s change that today, for tomorrow.
As of 2018, the Fortune 500 CEO list was only 6.6% women. To see real progress in STEM and particularly in AI, we need to create diversity in the field.
By creating a new generation of girls who are better suited for a career in science, beginning as early as age 7, we will see real change the world, one girl at a time!

data.title: Honda conducts successful launch and landing of experimental reusable rocket
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，本田研发公司成功进行了自主研发的可重复使用火箭的发射与着陆测试。火箭长6.3米，直径85厘米，干重900公斤，湿重1312公斤，在北海道大树町的本田设施内完成了测试。火箭升至271.4米高度，并在预定着陆点37厘米范围内成功着陆，飞行时长56.6秒。此次测试旨在验证火箭在升空和降落过程中的飞行稳定性及着陆能力，并收集了相关数据。本田自2024年起在大树町进行了多次安全测试，此次测试也采取了严格的安全措施，包括设立半径1公里的禁入区。本田希望通过研发可重复使用火箭，利用其核心技术为全球带来更多便利，并满足未来卫星发射需求的增长。

Topics
Honda Conducts Successful Launch and Landing Test of Experimental Reusable Rocket
TOKYO, Japan, June 17, 2025 â Honda R&D Co., Ltd., a research and development subsidiary of Honda Motor Co., Ltd., today conducted a launch and landing test of an experimental reusable rocket
*1
(6.3 m in length, 85 cm in diameter, 900 kg dry weight/1,312 kg wet weight) developed independently by Honda. The test was completed successfully, the first time Honda landed a rocket after reaching an altitude of nearly 300 meters.
This test marked the first launch and landing test conducted by Honda with an aim to demonstrate key technologies essential for rocket reusability, such as flight stability during ascent and descent, as well as landing capability. Through this successful test, Honda achieved its intended rocket behaviors for the launch and landing (reaching an altitude of 271.4 m, and landing within 37cm of the target touchdown point, with a flight duration of 56.6 sec), while obtaining data during the ascent and descent.

Test being conducted in Taiki Town in Hokkaido, Japan(Photo taken in May, 2025)
Launch and landing test
*1 A reusable rocket, also known as a reusable launch vehicle (RLV), is a type of rocket that, unlike a conventional expendable launch vehicle (ELV), can be used repeatedly in a short period of time. A reusable rocket is launched in a vertical position, reaches an altitude of around 100 kilometers, and then lands back on earth while maintaining a vertical position.

ï¼Safety measures for Honda rocket testingï¼
Since 2024, Honda has been safely conducting engine combustion tests and hovering tests for its reusable rockets in Taiki Town in Hiroo District, Hokkaido, Japan. As with all previous tests, Honda conducted this launch and landing test while placing the highest priority on safety and with the understanding and cooperation of local authorities and residents.Â
Specific safety measures taken for this test
A restricted area with a 1-kilometer radius was established. During the test, access to the area was restricted through the installation of signs and gates, as well as the deployment of security personnel.
The restricted area was defined by calculating the potential area where the rocket could fall to earth in the event of a thrust cut-off and by adding a sufficient buffer zone (safe distance calculated based on the guidelines set forth by the Cabinet Office of the Government of Japan) that would cover the potential area where a blast wave, debris dispersion, or fireballs could impact in the event of an explosion within the potential fall area.
The experimental rocket was equipped with a safety system to prevent deviation from a pre-defined flight corridor, speed and attitude conditions, ensuring no impact beyond the restricted area.

Examples of Honda initiatives toward creating new value in the ultimate environment of outer space include research into a circulative renewable energy system, key robotic technologies for use in outer space and reusable rockets.Â

data.title: After millions of years, why are carnivorous plants still so small?
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: carnivorous plants have been trapping animals for millions of years, but they have never evolved to become larger. These plants, which obtain nutrients by consuming insects and other small creatures, have independently evolved at least ten times in history. Despite their ability to thrive in nutrient-poor environments, carnivorous plants remain small. This is likely due to the trade-offs between the energy invested in capturing prey and the energy required for growth and survival. The limited size may also be a result of their specialized habitat requirements and the need to maintain efficient trapping mechanisms. Overall, their small stature persists as a successful evolutionary strategy.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： carnivorous plants的生物学特性、进化及其潜在的捕食能力

不同观点：
• IAmBroom认为，维纳斯捕蝇草适应了贫瘠的土壤环境，失去了对真菌的防御能力。当人类在土壤中添加营养物质时，这些植物因真菌感染而死亡。这种适应性使得它们在营养丰富的环境中反而无法生存。
• _tom_则提出反例，如能够困住羊的荆棘，表明有些植物确实能够从大型生物的死亡中获益，并用椰子树的例子进一步支持这一观点。
• jcalx引用了一个世界构建网站上的回答，描述了一种名为“骨草”的假想食肉植物，通过与真菌共生实现对动物的大规模捕杀，强调了植物与真菌或细菌共生的可能性。
• TheOtherHobbes分享了一个个人经历，维纳斯捕蝇草能够释放强烈吸引力，即使在封闭环境中也能吸引大量苍蝇，最终因捕食过量而死亡。
• bell-cot指出，当食肉植物大到足以捕食小型哺乳动物时，会遇到“妈妈熊障碍”，即母熊等动物会为了保护幼崽而摧毁植物，限制了植物的捕食能力。
• Nevermark认为植物间直接以物理结构为食的现象应该有特定的名称，并提出植物间竞争的例子，如榕树。
• almosthere提到许多食肉植物失去了部分或大部分叶绿体基因组，因为它们从动物中获取养分，不再需要光合作用，并认为食肉性可能是进化的“死胡同”。
• leoedin认为，随着猎物智商的提高，它们更容易识破植物的陷阱，因此食肉植物的捕猎效率受到限制。
• imoreno从进化角度分析，认为食肉植物的进化适应涉及多个因素，提出了“适应度超曲面”的概念，指出不同的小生态环境导致多样化的捕猎机制。
• Noelia-认为小型食肉植物通过巧妙的策略在贫瘠环境中生存，本身就是一种惊人的进化成就，而非必须变得巨大。
• chrisco255和mmsc以幽默的方式提及流行文化中的食肉植物，如《超级玛丽》中的蘑菇王国和《The Day of the Triffids》小说。
• phkahler补充，大型动物能够通过观察其他动物被捕食而学会避开陷阱，这限制了食肉植物捕猎大型猎物的能力。

补充讨论：

44271760.article_content:
Articles

June 6, 2025
Carnivorous Plants Have Been Trapping Animals for Millions of Years. So Why Have They Never Grown Larger?
Plants that feed on meat and animal droppings have evolved at least ten times through evolutionary history
A Cape sundew wraps its sticky leaves around a helpless fly.
Ben pcc via Wikipedia under CC By-SA 4.0
44271760.article_summary: carnivorous plants have been trapping animals for millions of years, but they have never evolved to become larger. These plants, which obtain nutrients by consuming insects and other small creatures, have independently evolved at least ten times in history. Despite their ability to thrive in nutrient-poor environments, carnivorous plants remain small. This is likely due to the trade-offs between the energy invested in capturing prey and the energy required for growth and survival. The limited size may also be a result of their specialized habitat requirements and the need to maintain efficient trapping mechanisms. Overall, their small stature persists as a successful evolutionary strategy.

data.title: Real-time action chunking with large models
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在机器人实时操作中使用大型视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）的挑战和解决方案。与聊天机器人或图像生成器不同，机器人必须实时运行，延迟会影响其表现。VLAs虽然能很好地泛化到开放世界，但因模型庞大、参数多，运行速度较慢，尤其在边缘设备上延迟更明显。为解决此问题，文章提出“动作分块”（Action Chunking）方法，即每次推理调用时输出并执行一系列动作。然而，简单分块可能导致动作不连续和不安全加速。为此，作者开发了“实时分块算法”（RTC），通过“冻结”部分前一块动作并填补新块剩余部分，解决了不连续性问题。实验表明，RTC显著加快了执行速度，即使在人为延迟情况下也能完成动态精确任务。

Real-Time Action Chunking with Large Models
Published
June 9, 2025
Email
research@physicalintelligence.company
Kevin Black, Manuel Y. Galliker, Sergey Levine
Paper
Unlike chatbots or image generators, robots must operate in
real time
. While a robot is “thinking”, the world around it
evolves according to physical laws, so delays between inputs and outputs have a tangible impact on performance. For a
language model, the difference between fast and slow generation is a satisfied or annoyed user; for a
vision-language-action model (VLA), it could be the difference between a robot handing you a hot coffee or spilling it in
your lap. While VLAs have achieved
promising results
in open-world
generalization, they can be slow to run. Like their cousins in language and vision, these models have billions of
parameters and require heavy-duty GPUs. On edge devices like mobile robots, that adds even more latency for network
communication between a centralized inference server and the robot
1
.
To build a
real-time system
with VLAs, we are going to need some form of asynchrony: that is, we must let a model think
about its future actions while executing a previous one.
Action chunking
— where a robot outputs and executes a
sequence of multiple actions for each inference call — provides a good starting point.
Our
VLAs
all use a chunk size of 50 actions, corresponding to 1 second of real time.
However, chunking alone is not enough. When we switch chunks, the new actions might not “agree” with the old ones,
causing discontinuities and unsafe accelerations. Trying to naively smooth over these discontinuities is not guaranteed
to produce valid actions, and can have disastrous consequences.
The aforementioned disastrous consequences. These results are obtained by
attempting to do real-time inference with temporal ensembling to smooth over the discontinuities, a popular prior method
introduced in
ACT
(Zhou et al., 2023).
As a result, in
π
0
,
π
0
-FAST, and
π
0.5
, we did not use a real-time strategy
2
. We executed actions
synchronously
,
meaning that we would finish executing one chunk, wait for model inference, and then begin executing the next one. This
way, the robot started each chunk from rest, and we circumvented the issues that arise from switching chunks
while in motion. However, this introduces pauses between chunks that are still harmful — these pauses aren't in
the training data. Not to mention: they slow things down, are ugly to look at, and discourage us from scaling up the size
of our models.
To solve these problems, we developed an algorithm that we call
real-time chunking
(RTC)
. It enables real-time
execution without discontinuities, and it works on any diffusion- or flow-based VLA — including
π
0.5
— with
no
training-time changes
. We found that RTC significantly sped up execution time for all the tasks we tested. It was also
very robust to latency, even when we injected artificial delays to cause much higher latencies than normal. RTC
completed dynamic and precise tasks, like striking a match or plugging in an Ethernet cable, with inference delays of
more than 300 milliseconds.
Thinking while moving
replay
Action chunk 1
Action chunk 2
When there is an inference delay, real-time execution requires careful consideration. While a new chunk is generated
(red), the previous chunk (green) continues executing. If the new chunk is substantially different — which it often is —
switching to the new chunk results in disaster.
The core challenge of real-time execution is to maintain consistency between action chunks. By the time a new chunk has
been generated by the model, the previous one has already been executed partway. Without a specialized algorithm, the new
chunk might be totally incompatible with the robot's current trajectory — the model might be reacting to new information,
or it might just be sampling a different “strategy” from its learned distribution of behaviors. Thus, we must somehow
use
the overlapping timesteps where we have access to the remaining actions of the previous chunk. A good real-time
algorithm should produce a new chunk that is
consistent
with these overlapping actions while still preserving the
model's reactivity to new information and ability to make intelligent decisions.
Our key insight is to pose real-time chunking as an inpainting problem. Let's say that our model takes 3 controller
timesteps to produce an action chunk after receiving an observation. The first 3 actions of a new chunk can't be
executed, since those timesteps will have already passed by the time the new chunk is available. Thus, it makes sense to
“freeze” those actions to the values from the previous chunk that we know
will
be executed; our goal is then to fill in
the remainder of the new chunk, much like inpainting a section of an image that has been removed. Depending on the chunk
size and how often we run inference, there will be some number of actions beyond the first 3 that also overlap with the
previous chunk. Ra

data.author: moelf
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Framework Laptop 12，这是一款模块化、可修复、可升级的笔记本电脑。其采用塑料外壳，提供五种双色选项，包括独特的紫色和泡泡糖色，使其外观更加亲和和与众不同。尽管塑料常被认为廉价，但Framework通过结合ABS塑料和TPU塑料，使机身坚固且耐冲击。键盘和触控板颜色选择有限，只有紫色款配有颜色匹配的触控板。该笔记本使用独特的扩展卡系统，允许用户自定义端口配置，但目前只有USB-C扩展卡有颜色选项。屏幕质量良好，但边框较厚，设计上仍有改进空间。总体而言，Laptop 12以其定制性和耐用性吸引特定用户群体。

"What's this purple laptop? It's cool."
Over a decade-plus of doing gadget reviews and review-adjacent things, my wife (and, lately, my 5-year-old) have mostly stopped commenting on the ever-shifting selection of laptops I have in my bag or lying around the house at any given time. Maybe she can't tell them apart, or maybe she just figures there isn't that much to say about whatever black or silver metal slab I'm carrying around. Either way, they practically never elicit any kind of response, unless there are just too many of them sitting out in too many places.
But she
did
ask about the Framework Laptop 12, the third and latest major design in Framework's slowly expanding lineup of modular, repairable, upgradeable laptops. With its five two-toned color options and sturdy plastic exterior, it's definitely more approachable and friendly-looking than the Laptop 13 or Laptop 16, both metal slabs with a somewhat less-finished and prototype-y look to them. But it retains the features that a certain kind of PC geek likes about Framework's other laptops—user-customizable and swappable ports, an easy-to-open design, first-class Linux support, and the promise of future upgrades that improve its performance and other specs.
Look and feel
The Laptop 12 stacked atop the Laptop 13.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Plastic gets a bad rap, and there are indeed many subpar plastic gadgets out there. When done poorly, plastic can look and feel cheap, resulting in less durable devices that show more wear over time.
But well-done plastic can still feel solid and high-quality, in addition to being easier to make in different colors. Framework says the Laptop 12's chassis is a combination of ABS plastic and
TPU plastic
(a more flexible, rubberized material), molded over a metal inner structure. The result is something that can probably actually take the shock of a drop or a fall better than many aluminum-and-glass laptops without feeling overly cheap or chintzy.
The five two-tone color options—the boring, businesslike black and gray, plus purple-and-gray lavender, pink-and-baby-blue bubblegum, and the green sage options—are the most fun thing about it, and the lavender and bubblegum colors are particularly eye-catching.
Keyboard and trackpad. Only the lavender and gray laptops get a color-matched trackpad; the keyboard and deck are always different shades of gray.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Matching other components to the exterior of the system can be a bit of a crapshoot, though. The screwdriver and spudger that Framework provides for upgrading and repairing all of its systems
does
match the color of the laptop, and the two-tone styluses for the touchscreens will also match the laptops when they're made available for purchase in the coming months.
The lavender option is the only one that can also be configured with a color-matched lavender trackpad—the only other trackpad option is gray, and the keyboard deck and the keyboard itself are all gray no matter what color laptop you pick. This is presumably meant to limit the number of different trackpad options that Framework has to manufacture and stock, but it is too bad that the laptop's keyboard and palm rest aren't as colorful as the rest of it.
The Laptop 12 also uses Framework's still-unique Expansion Card system for customizing the built-in ports. These are all 10 Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports rather than the Thunderbolt ports on the Intel versions of the Laptop 13, but all four support the same speeds, all four support charging, and all four support display output, so you really can put whatever port you want wherever you want it.
A downside of the Laptop 12 is that, as of this writing, only the USB-C Expansion Modules are available in color-matched versions. If you want USB-A, HDMI, DisplayPort, or any other kind of port on your system, you'll get the silver modules that were designed to match the finish on the Framework Laptops 13 and 16, so you'll have to put up with at least one mismatched port on your otherwise adorable system.
Only the USB-C Expansion Cards are available in lavender, which can make for goofy-looking mismatches. But I do prefer the Framework 16-style retention switches to the Framework Laptop 13's retention buttons, which you need to hold down as you pull out the Expansion Card.

Andrew Cunningham

MiniMax-M1
1. Model Overview
We introduce MiniMax-M1, the world's first open-weight, large-scale hybrid-attention reasoning model.
MiniMax-M1 is powered by a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture combined with a lightning
attention mechanism. The model is developed based on our previous
MiniMax-Text-01 model
,
which contains a total of 456 billion parameters with 45.9 billion parameters activated
per token. Consistent with MiniMax-Text-01, the M1 model natively supports a context length of 1
million tokens, 8x the context size of DeepSeek R1. Furthermore, the lightning attention mechanism
in MiniMax-M1 enables efficient scaling of test-time compute – For example, compared to DeepSeek
R1, M1 consumes 25% of the FLOPs at a generation length of 100K tokens. These properties make M1
particularly suitable for complex tasks that require processing long inputs and thinking extensively.
MiniMax-M1 is trained using large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) on diverse problems ranging from
traditional mathematical reasoning to sandbox-based, real-world software engineering environments.
We develop an efficient RL scaling framework for M1 highlighting two perspectives: (1) We propose
CISPO, a novel algorithm that clips importance sampling weights instead of token updates, which
outperforms other competitive RL variants; (2) Our hybrid-attention design naturally enhances the
efficiency of RL, where we address unique challenges when scaling RL with the hybrid architecture. We
train two versions of MiniMax-M1 models with
40K
and
80K
thinking budgets respectively. Experiments
on standard benchmarks show that our models outperform other strong open-weight models such as
the original DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-235B, particularly on complex software engineering, tool using,
and long context tasks. With efficient scaling of test-time compute, MiniMax-M1 serves as a strong
foundation for next-generation language model agents to reason and tackle real-world challenges.
Benchmark performance comparison of leading commercial and open-weight models across competition-level mathematics, coding, software engineering, agentic tool use, and long-context understanding tasks. We use the MiniMax-M1-80k model here for MiniMax-M1.

data.title: Reasoning by Superposition: A Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought
data.author: danielmorozoff
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了连续思维链（Chain of Continuous Thought, CoT）在推理问题中的理论基础，特别是针对有向图可达性问题。作者证明了具有连续CoT的两层Transformer可以在图的直径步数内解决该问题，而离散CoT则需要更多步骤。连续CoT通过超位置状态同时编码多个搜索前端，实现并行广度优先搜索，而离散CoT则需顺序搜索，可能陷入局部解。实验验证了理论结果，显示连续CoT在训练中自动涌现多路径探索能力。本文揭示了连续CoT在推理任务中优于离散CoT的原因。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in many applications, including challenging reasoning problems via chain-of-thoughts (CoTs) techniques that generate ``thinking tokens'' before answering the questions. While existing theoretical works demonstrate that CoTs with discrete tokens boost the capability of LLMs, recent work on continuous CoTs lacks a theoretical understanding of why it outperforms discrete counterparts in various reasoning tasks such as directed graph reachability, a fundamental graph reasoning problem that includes many practical domain applications as special cases. In this paper, we prove that a two-layer transformer with $D$ steps of continuous CoTs can solve the directed graph reachability problem, where $D$ is the diameter of the graph, while the best known result of constant-depth transformers with discrete CoTs requires $O(n^2)$ decoding steps where $n$ is the number of vertices ($D<n$). In our construction, each continuous thought vector is a superposition state that encodes multiple search frontiers simultaneously (i.e., parallel breadth-first search (BFS)), while discrete CoTs must choose a single path sampled from the superposition state, which leads to sequential search that requires many more steps and may be trapped into local solutions. We also performed extensive experiments to verify that our theoretical construction aligns well with the empirical solution obtained via training dynamics. Notably, encoding of multiple search frontiers as a superposition state automatically emerges in training continuous CoTs, without explicit supervision to guide the model to explore multiple paths simultaneously.

44309345.article_summary: 本文探讨了连续思维链（Chain of Continuous Thought, CoT）在推理问题中的理论基础，特别是针对有向图可达性问题。作者证明了具有连续CoT的两层Transformer可以在图的直径步数内解决该问题，而离散CoT则需要更多步骤。连续CoT通过超位置状态同时编码多个搜索前端，实现并行广度优先搜索，而离散CoT则需顺序搜索，可能陷入局部解。实验验证了理论结果，显示连续CoT在训练中自动涌现多路径探索能力。本文揭示了连续CoT在推理任务中优于离散CoT的原因。
44309345.comments_summary:

不同观点：

补充讨论：
• 该评论主要起到了信息分享的作用，指出了论文与FAIR先前工作的关联，但没有直接表达对论文内容或研究方法的具体评价。
• 链接指向了一篇24年12月发布的论文，暗示了该研究可能涉及前沿的人工智能领域，尤其是FAIR的相关研究方向。
• 没有出现对该论文或其前提研究的直接争议或批评，评论更多是提供信息以供感兴趣的人参考。

总结：评论的核心在于分享一篇论文及其与FAIR研究的关系，持正面态度并引导进一步阅读。没有明显争议，主要是信息共享和指引。

data.title: Scrappy – Make little apps for you and your friends
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了John和Pontus创建的原型工具Scrappy，旨在推动“自制软件”的理念，让个人能够为自己和亲友制作个性化、不求精美但满足特定需求的应用程序。Scrappy提供一个无限画布，用户可以通过拖放交互对象并附加简单代码来构建应用，类似于Figma等工具。文章通过几个例子展示了Scrappy的用途，如算术练习、参会人数计数器、会议成本计时器和家务分配表。Scrappy应用支持多人协作、持久化状态和选择性共享，且编辑和运行无明显区分。该项目旨在重新构想软件创作，鼓励普通用户通过“轻量编程”和“自制软件”表达自我，而不必成为专业程序员。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Scrappy及类似工具的可行性、使用场景、技术实现和社区影响的讨论

不同观点：
• RodgerTheGreat认为Scrappy与CardStock和Decker有相似之处，但CardStock是开源且可以本地运行的，Decker则提供了更强大的功能如表格数据处理和可重用的组件抽象。
• al_borland不看好Scrappy的托管解决方案，担心其长期依赖性和维护问题，倾向于使用HTML/CSS/JS和PHP等传统技术来实现简单项目，并强调工具的长期可用性。
• tokioyoyo分享了自己通过简单应用获得的成就感，认为即使没有经济收益，开发这样的应用也是值得的。
• simonw指出Scrappy在移动端编辑功能的缺失，并认为不应低估手机用户的需求，移动设备可能是他们唯一的计算工具。
• nilirl认为电子表格是最实用的终端用户编程环境，对Scrappy等新工具持保留态度。
• selcuka认为LLM（大语言模型）生成的简单应用可能会成为Scrappy等工具的强力竞争者，并提到LLM在生成简单HTML/JS应用上的潜力。
• Peteragain建议从家庭运行的小型应用商店入手，强调社区和朋友间的非正式分享，而不是追求商业化。
• blips对AI生成内容持负面态度，认为其影响了内容的吸引力，并表示不愿消费此类内容。
• riffraff支持“可脚本化的组件”而不是块状编程，并指出用户希望应用易于分享且零成本。
• indyjo对Scrappy的UI设计和编程支持提出质疑，认为缺乏代码补全和API帮助是其不足之处。
• feeley介绍了一个名为CodeBoot的替代工具，允许用户通过Python创建封装在URL中的Web应用，强调其易用性和无安装需求。
• zupa-hu认为Scrappy的演示很棒，但反馈过于苛刻，可能是因为其进入市场的时间较晚。
• hiAndrewQuinn分享了自己使用LLM和JavaScript等技术创建简单工具的经验，强调其跨平台性和易用性。
• kakamiokatsu认为Scrappy与Visual Basic有相似之处，特别是在简单原则和UI设计方面。
• s_ting765认为如果缺乏源代码分享功能，Scrappy的应用分享价值将大打折扣。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Scrappy等工具的长期可用性和维护问题，特别是托管解决方案的依赖性。
- 用户对移动端支持和易用性的需求被提出，特别是移动设备作为唯一计算工具的用户场景。
- 不同工具的对比，如CardStock、Decker和CodeBoot，提供了其他实现类似功能的选择。
- LLM在简单应用开发中的潜力被多次提及，可能成为未来竞争的一个重要因素。

44306859.article_content:
UPDATE:
Hello Hacker News!
Here’s an FAQ
for common questions not addressed in the article. We’ll keep updating it and eventually add it at the bottom of this page.
Software is important to people. Most of us spend our workdays in front of computers. We use the computer in our pocket tens if not hundreds of times every day. The apps we use are almost exclusively mass-market, sold on an app-store, made for thousands if not millions of users. Or they are enterprise apps that are custom-built for hundreds of thousands of dollars.
But there isnât really any equivalent of home-made software â apps made lovingly by you for your friends and family. Apps that arenât polished or flashy, but are made to
your
preference
and help you with
your particular needs.
Weâre John and Pontus, and weâve been exploring the potential of home-made software together.
We ended up creating a research prototype that we call
Scrappy
â a tool for making
scrappy apps for just you and your friends.
First and foremost, we aim to contribute a
vision
of what home-made software could be like. We want to make this vision as concrete as we can, by sharing a working tool and examples of apps made in it. Scrappy, in its current state, is a prototype, not a robust tool, but we hope it paints the picture we carry in our heads â of software as something that can be creative, personal, expressive. Made by anyone, for themselves and their loved ones.
What is Scrappy?
It may not be clear what âa scrappy app for you and your friendsâ means. What kind of apps are these? Let us paint a picture with a few examples. (We call them â
Scrapps
â.)
Arithmetic practice for a kid in elementary school.
When outgrown, the Scrapp can be extended with harder problems.
(
try on desktop
)
Attendee counter for a local event.
The counterâs state is shared, so the Scrapp can be used to let people in and out at multiple entrances.
(
try on desktop
)
Meeting cost clock,
to help meetings stay on track. A Scrapp like this can be put together in 15 minutes and shared with coworkers right away.
(
try on desktop
)
Weekly chore tracker.
Let roommates flexibly swap weeks, while making sure to track whose up next, to keep things fair.
(
try on desktop
)
What is it like to make an app in Scrappy?
Scrappy is an infinite canvas of interactive objects. The workflow is similar to an app such as Figma, Miro, or Google Slides â except you can attach behaviors to the objects.
You drag objects out on the canvas â a button, a textfield, a few labels. Select an object, and you can modify its attribute in an inspector panel. Certain objects, like buttons, has attributes like âwhen clickedâ that contain javascript code. When the button is clicked, that code is run â maybe it records the contents of the textfield to a label that acts as a log. You build your app step by step: tweaking and rearranging the objects, and attaching a little bit of code to them.
Thereâs no better way to get a feeling for an authoring environment than to see someone use it in action. In the following videos, Iâm making an attendee counter for an event.
The basics.
I start out by adding a number field to track the number of attendees, and two buttons for recording people entering and exiting the venue.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Reactive formulas.
Next, I add a field for the venueâs capacity, and a warning when too many people have been let in.
I use a reactive formula to control the visibility of the warning and the border color of the field.
Your browser cannot play this video.
A shared, persistent world.
Without any extra work, Scrappy apps are multiplayer.
App state is persisted and synced, like users expect from online documents like Google Sheets or Figma.
Your browser cannot play this video.
The app is always live.
Thereâs no distinction between editing and running. I can edit the app while a friend is using it.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Selective sharing.
I make a variant of the app thatâs limited to only entering and exiting people. This is done by putting a part of the app in a frame, and sharing only that frame. The limited version is still linked to the main app.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Visible, tangible data.
Hereâs what the
Meeting Cost Clock app
shown above looks like when zoomed out, revealing a common pattern in Scrapps.
Outside the shared frame are a bunch of fields used to compute the cost of the meeting. This lets me see the data while Iâm working on the Scrapp, just like in a spreadsheet, which is very helpful for debugging â and it makes future tweaking or remixing easier.
Why make Scrappy?
This project is driven by a desire to reimagine software creation and use. As part of a growing movement variously termed â
small computing
,â â
casual programming
â, and â
home-cooked software
â we want to
emancipate end-users
â to âempower people to express themselves without requiring them to be heavy-duty progra

data.title: Locally hosting an internet-connected server
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到用户被随机选中进行CAPTCHA验证以确认请求。页面提供了一个登录表单，包括账号、密码输入框以及“记住我”选项。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的替代选项。用户需完成CAPTCHA验证才能继续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决ISP在IPv6支持不足的情况下进行网络配置，以及使用不同工具和方法实现网络路由和IP分配。

不同观点：
• [JdeBP] 认为许多北美和西欧的ISP在2025年仍不擅长提供IPv6支持，用户不得不自行解决此问题，例如通过复杂的设置来绕过ISP的限制。他还指出，一些ISP多年来一直承诺提供IPv6但未实现。
• [Daviey] 建议使用Tailscale或Headscale处理WireGuard和低层网络配置，而不是手动管理iptables和低层组件，并分享了自己的成功经验，包括可以轻松添加设备和使用出口IP池。
• [DougN7] 提出使用动态DNS服务（如dyn.com）作为解决方案，并指出许多家庭路由器内置支持动态DNS。
• [KronisLV] 表示自己选择了Tailscale以避免手动管理WireGuard和iptables，并提到SSH隧道的不足之处。
• [PeterStuer] 分享了自己使用Pangolin和Traefik进行Wireguard隧道设置的经验，并提供了一个参考链接。

补充讨论：
• [varenc] 对Monkeybrains ISP用户能获得对称600Mbps的连接表示好奇，并分享了自己的多WAN网关设置以提高连接稳定性，同时提供了自己的网络延迟日志对比。
• [zokier] 建议如果不希望在所有服务器上运行Wireguard，可以设置一个集中式的Wireguard网关，并提供了一些自动化脚本的参考链接。
• [xiconfjs] 引用Monkeybrains ISP的安装条件，提到安全访问屋顶是成功安装的一个因素。
• [anonymousiam] 分享了自己20年前使用vtun绕过住宅静态IP限制的经验，并比较了当时FiOS和VPS的费用。
• [politelemon] 提出Cloudflare隧道作为另一种选择，通过在其控制面板上设置DNS和安装其Daemon来避免打开外部端口。
• [zrm] 认为大多数情况下不需要多个公共IPv4地址，可以通过端口映射和反向代理来实现多个服务的公开，并讨论了使用VPN的方案。
• [eqvinox] 建议了解VRFs并应用于策略路由，认为这是更好的一种封装方式。
• [dismalpedigree] 分享了自己使用Nebula网络和haproxy进行加密数据传输的设置，强调了无密钥的vps设置和跨地域的节点部署。
• [v5v3] 建议在文章中添加警告，提醒新手在开放服务器之前需要进行基本的网络安全设置。
• [bzmrgonz] 提出安装反向代理和使用Wireguard重定向非静态IP服务的可能性，并询问潜在风险。

争议焦点：
• ISP在IPv6支持上的不足以及用户自行解决的必要性。
• 使用不同工具（如Tailscale、动态DNS、Cloudflare隧道）的优劣比较。
• 是否需要多个公共IPv4地址以及如何通过反向代理和端口映射来优化配置。

data.article_summary: Terpstra Keyboard WebApp是一个用于调音和布局的在线工具，支持多种音律系统和布局方式，如Jankó、Harmonic Table、Wicki-Hayden、B-System、C-System等。用户可以选择预设，调整参数如基本频率、步长、旋转角度等，并使用不同的乐器音色。该应用还支持自定义音阶、颜色布局和空白键等功能。著名的31-ed2 Bosanquet/Wilson/Terpstra音律也在支持之列，包含详细的音阶和音名列表。该WebApp由Siemen Terpstra设计，James Fenn等开发，并以GPL-3.0协议开源发布。

data.title: The Grug Brained Developer (2022)
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 《Grug Brained Developer》是一本以幽默方式撰写的软件开发指南，作者自称为“Grug大脑开发者”，意指思维简单但经验丰富的程序员。Grug承认自己并不聪明，但在多年编程中积累了一些经验和教训。他强调复杂性是软件开发的天敌，像恶魔一样潜入代码库，导致问题。Grug建议用“不”来抵制不必要的功能和复杂性，以保持项目的简洁。然而，在现实中，为了职业发展和生活需求，开发者有时需要妥协说“好”。在编码时，Grug主张延迟代码的重构，直到项目有了一定形状和理解，以避免过早抽象。最终，Grug的目标是通过分享自己的错误和经验，帮助其他开发者享受编程并避免复杂性恶魔的陷阱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的复杂性与简化，以及调试工具和开发哲学的选择

不同观点：
• **调试工具的选择与使用**：[titanomachy] 认为使用调试器是理解系统的最佳方式，但在实际工作中（尤其是网页技术领域），大多数人依赖打印语句调试。他尝试让团队其他成员采用他的工作流但未成功。这表明开发者在调试工具的选择上存在分歧，部分人偏好简单直接的调试方法。

• **复杂性与简化的权衡**：[prmph] 和 [GMoromisato] 强调复杂性通常是不必要的，会带来额外的问题。他们通过具体例子（如简化类型系统和去除不必要的工具）说明简化代码和工作流的好处。然而，[GMoromisato] 也指出，复杂性在某些情况下是不可避免且有价值的，关键在于选择合适的时机引入复杂性。[dgb23] 补充，有经验的开发者能够处理复杂性但选择不引入不必要的复杂性，这是合理的建议。

• **复杂性的定义和理解**：[osigurdson] 质疑“复杂性”的定义，认为缺乏对复杂性的共同理解可能导致误解。例如，多文件项目是否被视为复杂取决于开发者的经验和熟悉程度。[0xbadcafebee] 进一步指出，复杂性不是单一的概念，有时它是必要且有价值的，开发者应避免的是不必要的复杂性。

• **开发哲学与职业建议**：[minkzilla] 提出了一种讽刺性的职业建议，即学会说“是”，然后将失败归咎于他人，这是对某些企业文化中技术决策和沟通问题的批评。[1-more] 则以幽默的方式表达了对静态类型、纯函数式语言的偏好，认为这些语言通过类型系统和编译器帮助开发者管理复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **技术崇拜与工具选择**：[butterlesstoast] 表达了对教授Carson和HTMX技术的感激，表明某些技术或工具在不同阶段的学习和应用中可能被低估，但在实际工作中能展现其价值。

• **历史视角与文化影响**：[dmurray] 提到这篇文章可能早在十年前就已存在，表明这种开发哲学和讨论在软件开发社区中具有长期的影响和共鸣。

争议焦点：
• **复杂性的价值与危害**：部分开发者认为复杂性在某些情况下是必要且有价值的，而另一些开发者则认为应尽可能简化系统和代码，以避免不必要的问题。这种对复杂性的不同看法反映了开发者在设计和实现系统时的不同优先级和价值观。

• **复杂性的定义和理解**：[osigurdson] 质疑“复杂性”的定义，认为缺乏对复杂性的共同理解可能导致误解。例如，多文件项目是否被视为复杂取决于开发者的经验和熟悉程度。[0xbadcafebee] 进一步指出，复杂性不是单一的概念，有时它是必要且有价值的，开发者应避免的是不必要的复杂性。

• **开发哲学与职业建议**：[minkzilla] 提出了一种讽刺性的职业建议，即学会说“是”，然后将失败归咎于他人，这是对某些企业文化中技术决策和沟通问题的批评。[1-more] 则以幽默的方式表达了对静态类型、纯函数式语言的偏好，认为这些语言通过类型系统和编译器帮助开发者管理复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **技术崇拜与工具选择**：[butterlesstoast] 表达了对教授Carson和HTMX技术的感激，表明某些技术或工具在不同阶段的学习和应用中可能被低估，但在实际工作中能展现其价值。

• **历史视角与文化影响**：[dmurray] 提到这篇文章可能早在十年前就已存在，表明这种开发哲学和讨论在软件开发社区中具有长期的影响和共鸣。

争议焦点：
• **复杂性的价值与危害**：部分开发者认为复杂性在某些情况下是必要且有价值的，而另一些开发者则认为应尽可能简化系统和代码，以避免不必要的问题。这种对复杂性的不同看法反映了开发者在设计和实现系统时的不同优先级和价值观。

data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者利用机器学习技术统计蒙古国境内所有蒙古包（ger）数量的过程。作者受到一篇关于蒙古帝国历史的播客启发，对当代蒙古社会产生兴趣，尤其是通过Google Maps卫星视图观察到首都乌兰巴托周围大量蒙古包。由于缺乏现成的数据，作者决定自行统计，设计了一个通过训练机器学习模型来识别和计数蒙古包的方案。他使用Google Maps下载卫星图像瓦片作为训练数据，手动标注蒙古包位置，并尝试训练模型进行自动识别。最终，作者详细描述了数据下载、标注过程及模型训练的基本步骤，并计划进一步探究这些蒙古包背后的社会故事。

I counted all of the yurts in Mongolia using machine learning
Jun 17, 2025
Table of Contents
The
Fall of Civilizations
podcast put out a
6¾-hour episode
on the history of the Mongol Empire, which I eagerly listened to. After finishing the episode I wondered
about contemporary Mongolian society, I wanted to learn what the lands that the Mongol Empire
exploded from are like in our current day. There are many ways to try to understand a society,
whether it be quantifying it or looking at the lived experiences within it. If you look at
data provided by the World Bank, you’ll see a country that has rapidly reduced poverty in the 21st
century, has a high economic growth rate, a healthy fertility rate, and is solidly an
upper-middle-income country. While Mongolia is a republic with a competitive party system,
Worldwide Governance Indicators
from the World Bank show a government that has issues with corruption, regulatory quality, and effectiveness.

(“Mongolia”)
All of these indicators are interesting to look at, but they don’t really show what a society is
like. I feel you get much more understanding by going to a country, walking the streets, and
talking to people there. If you’re unable to do this, the next best thing is spending hours
exploring Google Maps, which I did. I opened a satellite view of Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia.
I saw new glass buildings, Soviet-designed apartment blocks (called ugsarmal), impressive government
buildings, factories, and industrial areas. But something stood out to me. Yurts, extending for kilometers
in all directions.
Maps Data: Google © 2025 Airbus, CNES / Airbus, Maxar Technologies
Naturally, I was impressed by the quantity of yurts I saw, and I was curious: just how many yurts (ger in Mongolian) are in
Mongolia and why? This set me on the path drawing bounding boxes on over 10,000 yurts to train a machine learning
model to count the rest of the yurts in the country. While I was training the model, I wondered what
the story behind these yurts are, I did a small investigation for later in this article. For now,
this is the story of counting them.
Counting all the yurts in Mongolia
I was unable to find a count of the yurts in Mongolia, this left me with
the task of doing it myself. Although I had never studied or worked with machine learning, I knew
through some osmosis that machine learning is well fit for this task. I created a simple plan in my
brain:
Train a model to identify yurts
Reduce input space and parallelize searching of input space
Keep track of the yurts found
Training a model to identify yurts
The first thing I needed was training data, and lots of it. There’s many different options for satellite
imagery such as
Mapbox
,
Google Maps
,
and
ArcGIS
. I
decided to use Google Maps since I’m already familiar with it.
For digital maps, many systems break the world up into a series of 256 x 256 tiles identified by X, Y, Z values. This is
referred to as tiled web maps and allows for progressively loading maps at different zoom levels and
positions. The zoom level values tend to be 0 through 20, where 0 has the least tiles and 20 the
most. The formula for calculating the number of tiles at a given zoom (z) level is:
$2^z * 2^z$
.
This means increasing
z
by one will increase the tile count by four times.
I wrote a Python script that generated tiles from a box around Ulaanbaatar and downloaded
them to a folder to use as training data. To list the tiles inside a bounding box made up of a
southwest and northeast coordinates, I used the
mercantile package
.

Tiles from Google Maps, you can see yurts on the right tile. Maps Data: Google © 2025 Airbus, CNES / Airbus, Maxar Technologies
I decided to start at zoom level
17
as it is the lowest zoom level that I can still identify yurts
at. Once I downloaded several hundred tiles at this zoom level, I needed a way to label the yurts on
these tiles. Labeling is the process of drawing boxes around objects in an image. The idea is to
draw these boxes manually, creating what is called annotated data, and then training a model to do
the labeling using the annotated data.
There’s an open source tool called

this.

不同观点：

• **SpikedCola和samschooler**：指出网站链接错误问题，SpikedCola提到特定页面的logo链接404错误，samschooler确认了该问题并提供了另一个404链接。
• **godzillabrennus**：分享其在AI生成代码项目中的使用体验，表示会继续观察并反馈。

• **prophesi**：关注产品的开源性以及MCP服务器是否可以在本地沙箱环境中运行。

data.title: OpenSERDES – Open Hardware Serializer/Deserializer (SerDes) in Verilog (2020)
data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: OpenSERDES 是一个使用 Skywater Open PDK 130nm 技术实现的数字化可合成串行解串器（SerDes）架构。SerDes 将并行数据转换为串行数据传输，并通过高速度接口（如 LVDS）发送至接收端，再转换回并行数据。项目使用 OpenLane 和 Virtuoso Cadence 工具，Verilog HDL 编写，包含串行器、解串器、时钟数据恢复（CDR）、CMOS 反相器等模块。TX 驱动使用 CMOS 反相器链，RX 使用电阻反馈反相器和 CMOS 反相器设计，数据采样通过 DFF 实现，并采用过采样 CDR 恢复数据和时钟。项目文件包括 GDS、SPICE 和网表等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源芯片设计的可行性及挑战

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为开源CPU设计本身并不难，但要让芯片实际运行并与外部设备交互则非常困难。他指出，行业内大量使用预验证的模块化设计，如USB主机控制器、声音芯片、DRAM控制器和PCIe模块。他认为这是一个巨大的进步，但需要反复构建、表征和调整，才能让开源芯片真正自立。

• [gchadwick] 关注芯片设计中的细节问题，特别是模拟仿真中难以触发的事件在实际硅片运行中可能频繁发生，从而影响芯片功能。他强调了设备表征的重要性，并对是否有进行过tape out表示好奇。他同时也肯定了开源工具和PDK的可用性。

补充讨论：
• [peter_d_sherman] 提供了一本相关书籍《High-Speed Serial I/O Made Simple: A Designers’ Guide, with FPGA Applications》，作为进一步了解高速串行I/O设计的资源。

争议焦点：
• 开源芯片设计是否能够真正实现并与商业设计竞争。主要争议在于预验证模块化设计的广泛使用与开源设计需要反复调整的现实之间的差距。

总结：
讨论围绕开源芯片设计的复杂性及其面临的技术挑战展开，参与者普遍认可其潜在价值，但对其当前实现能力和实际应用效果存在一定质疑。

OpenSERDES
Serializer/Deserializer (
SerDes
) is the most important functional block used in high speed communication.
SerDes converts parallel data into a serial (one bit) stream of data that is transmitted over a high-speed connection, such as LVDS, to a receiver that converts the serial stream back to the original, parallel data.
A global CLOCK signal is present to sequence the serialization and deserialization of data from one block to another.
Technology:
Skywater OpenPDK 130nm
Tools Used:
OpenLane, Virtuoso Cadence
The
Serializer
and
Deserializer
blocks are coded in Verilog HDL and synthesized using Openlane tool mapped to Sky130 CMOS technology. Simulation results and associated gds, spice and netlist files are uploaded in Serializer and Deserializer folders respectively
A chain of CMOS inverters is used as TX driver to drive the input capacitance of the channel. The gds, spice, netlist and. oa files for the same are present in
Inverter_Based_Tx
folder
A fully synthesizable Rx is designed using Resistive FB inverter followed by CMOS inverter as sensing and gain element respectively. The following DFF is used to sample the data using the clock recovered by the CDR.
Resistive Feedback inverter
is used as sensing element to sense low amplitude received signal at the front end of the receiver. Details of the implementation of Resistive FB inverter can be found in Resistive_FB_inverter folder
DFF is the simplest memory block to sample and store the data before deserializing. Master Slave DFF is implemented using NAND logic gates. Details of the same are present in
DFF
and
NAND
folders
Oversampling CDR
is used to recover the data and clock from the received signal. The CDR uses the data transitions to tune the clock frequency for proper decoding of received signal. The
Oversampling_CDR
folder contains the gds, spice and synthesized Verilog files generated from Openlane tool.

data.title: Time Series Forecasting with Graph Transformers
data.author: turntable_pride
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了基于图结构数据的时序预测，特别关注利用图变换器（Graph Transformers）进行预测，并区分预测性范式和生成性范式。与传统方法不同，本文方法不仅关注单一的时间序列，还结合了相关数据源的信息，如营销活动、竞争对手定价和经济指标等，这些信息通过关系数据库中的表间关系自然形成图结构。文章介绍了一种从关系数据库自动发现和利用跨表关系的方法（RDL），将关系数据转化为图结构，从而将时序预测任务转化为图学习任务。文中详细描述了图预测框架，包括节点特征、时间频率编码、日历特征等输入信号，并通过多层感知机（MLP）等模型进行预测。这种方法能够更好地捕捉季节性效应和特殊日期特征，适用于实际业务中的多种预测任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于博客文章中提出的图变换器（graph transformers）在时间序列任务中有效性的争论，以及相关商业应用和学术推广的潜在冲突。

不同观点：
• **cye131** 认为博客文章中将图变换器作为标准或有效的时间序列方法是不准确的。他们指出，变换器（transformers）在时间序列任务中表现不佳，而图深度学习在缺乏真实行为或物理边界的任务中效果也不好。因此，将两者结合用于商业应用（如销售预测）的有效性存疑。cye131 提供了相关研究论文（https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.13504）作为证据，并提到许多研究表明基于变换器的模型通常不如更简单的模型（如提升树）有效。此外，cye131 质疑该博客文章背后公司同时进行学术推广和商业销售的行为，认为存在利益冲突。

44301998.article_content:
Time series forecasting is a cornerstone in modern business analytics, whether it is concerned with anticipating market trends, user behavior, optimizing resource allocation, or planning for future growth. As such, a wide range of different approaches have been introduced and investigated for forecasting, lately data-driven approaches using machine learning and generative models.
This blog post will dive into forecasting on graph structured entities,
e.g.
, as obtained from a relational database, utilizing not only the individual time series as signal but also related information. As most of the world’s data is stored in relational structures, this topic is of particular interest for real world applications. We describe an end-to-end pipeline to perform forecasting using graph transformers and specifically discuss predictive vs. generative paradigms.
Forecasting on Graph-structured Data
Forecasting is the process of making predictions about future events based on historical data and current observations, requiring detecting patterns, trends, and seasonal variations.
Traditional forecasting methods often treat time series data in isolation, focusing solely on temporal patterns within a single sequence. However, in real-world applications, valuable predictive signals often exist in related data sources. For instance, when forecasting product sales, factors such as marketing campaigns, competitor pricing, or regional economic indicators can significantly impact the accuracy of predictions. Graphs are a natural structure to represent such inter-connected data sources. They represent a set of inter-connected nodes of different entities, where some entities can have time series that can be forecasted. Each node can potentially hold a variety of features that hold important signal for forecasting tasks on other nodes. Further, they lend themselves to a wide arrange of machine learning methods,
e.g.
,
Graph Transformers
.
A prominent option for obtaining graphs directly from an underlying business problem on a relational database is
Relational Deep Learning (RDL)
, which automatically discovers and utilizes cross-table relationships and data in connected tables. The RDL scheme allows to automatically extract a graph structure from the relational database, allowing us to treat timeseries forecasting as a graph learning task. We will use the graph obtained via RDL as an example below. However, our graph forecasting techniques are not limited to graphs obtained via RDL but can be applied on arbitrary forecasting tasks where time series have to be forecasted for a subset of graph nodes.
Example.
Consider the task of forecasting the sales per day for all products stored in a product table (yellow). Further tables containing transactions (blue), customers (green), product marketing (red) can provide additional signals that help solving the task. Using the RDL scheme, we can automatically transform the relational tables into a graph with node features. Then, the task is to perform forecasting on the subset of product nodes via graph machine learning.

data.title: LLMs pose an interesting problem for DSL designers
data.author: gopiandcode
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在LLM（大型语言模型）时代，编程语言设计（尤其是领域特定语言DSL的设计）面临的挑战和未来可能性。作者指出，精心设计的编程语言或DSL可以减少样板代码，降低错误风险，并让开发者专注于解决更复杂的问题。然而，随着LLM的广泛应用，开发者开始依赖这些模型自动生成代码，从而可能减少对DSL设计和创新的需求。文章提到，LLM在常见语言（如Python）上表现优异，但在小众或特定领域语言上表现较差。作者担心LLM的发展可能会削弱DSL的吸引力，并呼吁探讨如何让语言设计与LLM协同发展，而不是被其取代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编码中的应用及其对DSL（领域特定语言）的影响

不同观点：
• **LLM引发技术栈固化的担忧**：
  - [romaniv] 认为LLM在编码中的推广基于一系列承诺，但这些承诺在技术被社会采用后迅速被推翻。例如，LLM最初声称每个人都可以轻松编码，但现在要求用户学习专门的提示技巧和测试生成代码。此外，LLM被认为能够理解现有代码，但现在却要求用户改变代码以适应LLM。
  - [NiloCK] 也观察到LLM可能导致技术栈固化，特别是在处理不同版本的API时，LLM倾向于使用训练数据中更常见的版本，而不是最新的API。
  
• **DSL的价值与必要性**：
  - [darepublic] 对DSL持怀疑态度，认为DSL的泛滥增加了复杂性，LLM可以帮助抑制一些不必要的DSL的增长。
  - [jo32] 认为在LLM时代，构建新的DSL是不必要的，因为现代语言模型已经能够处理主流语言，并且这些语言的工具链更为成熟。
  - [efitz] 直言不讳地表示不喜欢DSL，认为它们给新加入项目的成员带来了学习负担，并可能成为“只写”语言。
